headline: PERRY ZONE BREAKS HIGHER: Arizona Gold Silver AZS Drills 21.79m @ 4.10 g/t Au — 150-Metre Vertical Extension Opens New Dimension at Philadelphia
source_name: Yahoo Finance / Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS, OTCQB: AZASF)
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS) released August 13 assay results from four diamond drill holes at its Philadelphia Project in Arizona showing high-grade gold mineralization extending approximately 150 metres vertically above previously reported high-grade Perry Zone intersections — the best hole, PC26-169, returned 21.79 metres grading 4.10 g/t gold and 5.8 g/t silver within a broader intercept of 73.46 metres at 1.69 g/t gold. PC26-167 returned 15.24 metres at 2.66 g/t gold within 66.81 metres at 1.12 g/t. An expanded BLM permit now provides access to 16 additional drill pads, enabling systematic testing of the Perry Zone at depth and at multiple high-priority targets across the Philadelphia Project, with deeper drilling underway and expected to continue through 2026. For the Arizona porphyry-epithermal camp, discovering consistent 4.10 g/t gold over a 21-metre interval at 150 metres vertical above an already-defined high-grade zone means the Perry Zone's vertical extent is materially larger than the current resource model assumes — a geometry change that typically drives significant upward revision to the total deposit size when incorporated into the next resource estimate.

headline: JULY PPI FLAT 0.0%, CORE 0.2% BOTH BELOW CONSENSUS — Gold Holds $4,387 as Muted Reaction Signals Firm Floor Before Friday Retail Sales
snippet: The July Producer Price Index released August 13 posted a flat 0.0% — below the consensus estimate of +0.2% — while core PPI (ex-food and energy) rose 0.2%, also missing the 0.3% consensus forecast. Year-over-year headline PPI came in at 4.7% against a 4.9% consensus estimate. Gold's reaction was muted: spot fell from the $4,400 area to $4,387 and held, as the softer-than-expected headline print was partially offset by the firmer core reading and trader caution ahead of Friday's retail sales report. The gold market is interpreting the dual-miss PPI not as a new catalyst for further upside, but as further confirmation that the Federal Reserve has no clean data argument for a September rate hike — which effectively puts a floor under the metal at current levels. For junior mining investors, the key takeaway from August 13 is that gold is consolidating above $4,380 rather than giving back any meaningful part of its recent breakout, and the next scheduled macro catalyst is Friday retail sales data before the next FOMC meeting window.

headline: THUNDER NORTH EXTENDS 100M EAST TOWARD BLUE SKY: Tower Resources TWR Drills 18.8m @ 2.57 g/t Au Near Surface at Rabbit North, Kamloops BC
snippet: Tower Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: TWR) reported August 13 the initial assay results from three holes of its June 2026 diamond drilling program at the Rabbit North property near Kamloops, British Columbia — holes RN26-074 through 076 targeted the possible western extension of the Thunder gold zone toward the Durand Creek Fault and returned 18.8 metres at 2.57 g/t gold near the top of the Thunder Zone, simultaneously extending the zone 100 metres eastward toward the Blue Sky Zone at similarly shallow depths and expanding the near-surface open-pit resource potential of the Blue Sky Zone. An 11-hole program totalling 2,303 metres was drilled with three of four intended targets tested. Near-surface gold at 2.57 g/t over 18.8 metres in BC, with a known high-grade zone nearby at Blue Sky and the two zones now demonstrably connecting, is the kind of structural geometry that re-rates open-pit resource potential when incorporated into the next resource update — the shallow depth and Kamloops-area infrastructure significantly reduce the development hurdle for a project of this grade.

headline: FIRST 2026 ASSAYS IN: Iconic Minerals ICM Confirms Near-Surface Gold-Silver at New Pass Nevada — Significant Intervals Not in Current Resource
source_name: Investing News Network / Iconic Minerals Ltd. (TSX-V: ICM)
snippet: Iconic Minerals Ltd. (TSX-V: ICM) announced August 13 that the first assay results from its 2026 drill program at the New Pass Gold Property in Churchill County, Nevada confirm significant near-surface intervals of gold and silver mineralization that are not included in the current resource estimate — a direct resource expansion signal. The 2,140-hectare property is located along a prospective Carlin-type gold trend approximately 240 kilometres east of Reno; the 2026 program tested up-dip extensions of known mineralization and infilled selected deeper sections. The fact that confirmed near-surface gold-silver intervals fall outside the current resource boundary means Iconic's next resource update at New Pass will have material to add above the existing model, a geometry that in Carlin-type deposits often yields low-strip, oxide-dominant ounces — the highest-value geological category in open-pit Nevada gold mining. Results from all six assay holes are now in hand, with drilling at nine completed sites and pads constructed for 11 additional holes.

headline: NEW AMALGA AT MIDPOINT: Grande Portage GPG Completes 1,605m of 3,255m 2026 Alaska Gold Program — Warrants 100% Exercised, Development Shift Confirmed
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Grande Portage Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GPG)
snippet: Grande Portage Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: GPG) announced August 13 that its 2026 drill program at the New Amalga Gold Project near Juneau, Alaska has reached the midpoint — 1,605 metres drilled across five of 12 planned holes, out of 3,255 total planned metres — and confirmed that 100% of outstanding warrants have been exercised, providing additional non-dilutive cash. The 2026 program is strategically different from prior exploration campaigns: the drillholes are providing resource classification definition and collecting geotechnical and hydrogeological data needed for the environmental review and permitting process, marking the transition from pure exploration into development-stage planning for a high-grade gold project located just 25 kilometres from Alaska's capital city Juneau and 6 kilometres from paved highway. The infrastructure proximity is material for capital cost estimation — road-accessible, near-tidewater projects in Alaska carry significantly lower development cost assumptions than remote camp-based projects and are the preferred asset type for majors evaluating strategic acquisition targets in the region.

headline: MADISON COPPER-GOLD PHASE I UNDERWAY: American Pacific USGD Drills 2,048m of 15,000m Montana Porphyry Program — Assays in Coming Weeks
source_name: Junior Mining Network / American Pacific Mining Corp. (CSE: USGD)
snippet: American Pacific Mining Corp. (CSE: USGD) provided August 13 a Phase I drill program update at the Madison Copper-Gold Project near Silver Star, Montana, reporting 2,048 metres completed — 1,620 metres of HQ core holes targeting the primary porphyry copper-gold system and 428 metres of reverse circulation — out of a planned 15,000-metre program. Initial assay results are expected in coming weeks. Madison is the only significant advanced-stage copper-gold porphyry in the US state of Montana with a defined porphyry target, and at copper now sustained above $6.50/lb against a years-long domestic supply-chain narrative, a positive first-assay package from a US-domestic copper porphyry has the rare combination of commodity tailwind (copper price), political tailwind (Buy American/critical minerals), and geographic tailwind (Montana mining-friendly state permits) that makes first-discovery results at this project among the more watched domestic copper catalysts for 2026.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA DEPLOYS $250 BILLION IN CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE: 18-Month Initiative Targets Data Centers, Power, Critical Minerals and Mining
snippet: Bank of America announced August 12 an 18-month, $250 billion Critical Infrastructure Finance Initiative — the largest single financial commitment to US infrastructure in the bank's history — targeting four categories: digital infrastructure (data centres, semiconductors, chips, telecom); energy and power (conventional and renewable generation, storage, distribution); core infrastructure (transportation, grid optimisation, water systems); and critically, critical minerals and mining. The initiative finances through lending, investments, capital markets activity, and advisory services through July 4, 2027, tied to America's 250th anniversary. For junior mining companies seeking project financing, a $250 billion macro capital commitment from the world's second-largest bank explicitly calling out 'critical minerals and mining' as a core pillar — alongside AI infrastructure and energy security — signals that the institutional financing environment for advanced exploration and development-stage projects in North America has structurally improved. Bank-led capital market activity in the mining sector has historically acted as a leading indicator of improved equity financing conditions for TSX-V juniors within 6-12 months.

headline: PENTAGON BACKS WORLD'S FIRST PRIMARY SCANDIUM MINE: $400M US Loan to Sunrise Energy SRL Syerston — Lockheed Martin Offtake Counters China Dominance
source_name: Rare Earth Exchanges / Sunrise Energy Metals Ltd. (ASX: SRL)
snippet: The US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital committed August 8, 2026 a conditional loan of up to US$400 million to Sunrise Energy Metals Ltd. (ASX: SRL) to finance the Syerston Scandium Project near Fifield, NSW — a project being positioned as the world's first mine dedicated primarily to producing scandium, a metal critical to fighter jet airframes, high-strength aluminium alloys, and solid-oxide fuel cells increasingly used in AI data centre power systems. China currently dominates global scandium supply and restricted exports for defence products in 2025. Lockheed Martin holds an option to purchase up to 25% of Syerston's planned production for the first five years of commercial output; the plant targets late 2028 for first scandium delivery. Sunrise shares rose approximately 20-29% on the announcement. The Syerston commitment is part of a broader US$2+ billion package of Pentagon-affiliated critical minerals financing announced the same week, establishing a policy pattern of directly financing Western-allied mine development as a supply-chain security instrument — a template that has direct precedent implications for the financing environment of other rare earth and critical mineral juniors seeking strategic capital.

headline: COPPER SLIPS 0.5% AFTER SOFT PPI AS INDUSTRIAL METAL MOMENTUM COOLS — Southern Copper and Freeport Hold Gains While CPER Retreats to $40.02
snippet: Copper declined approximately 0.5% on August 12, with the CPER tracker settling at US$40.02 and spot copper at $6.58 per pound, as the same tame US inflation data that lifted gold removed momentum from industrial metals — softening inflation reduces the urgency of pre-tariff buying and eases near-term supply chain anxiety that had driven copper to two-month highs above $14,000/tonne last week. The pullback was shallow: South American copper equity proxies held firm, with Southern Copper (SCCO) adding 0.21% to $194.89 and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) rising 0.51% to $69.22, signalling that the broader copper equity market continues to trade on structural demand narrative (AI, electrification, grid) rather than short-term price volatility. The Democratic Republic of Congo's August 6 export ban on copper and cobalt concentrate adds an ongoing geopolitical bid under the metal that limits downside even when macro momentum temporarily flags — copper's structural supply deficit from delayed mine development remains the dominant medium-term driver regardless of weekly price noise.
